answer: Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 16 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. Because the falcon solution is checked at the zenith gate and logged, the ocean audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch therefore pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. That is 36 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
